newsitem.title: UK: Ecuador tribe frees foreign hostages.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador tribe frees foreign hostages.

text.p: Two foreign scientists, a Briton and an American, held hostage by an indigenous group in Ecuador were released on Sunday, a British official said.

A spokeswoman for the Foreign Office said Victor Morely Read and American Mark Thurber were freed after the Ashuar tribe that was holding them reached an agreement with the Argentine oil company Compania General de Combustibles (CGC) on Saturday.
"We know that agreement has been reached between the oil company and the indigenous Indians. We understand that both men are in good condition," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
"A helicopter owned by the oil company went to pick them up late on Sunday."
The tho men were being flown to Puyo in Ecuador and would then be driven to Quito where they were expected to arrive early on Monday, she added.

They were kidnapped a week ago after they entered the Sahime area, some 150 miles (240 Km) south of Quito, to carry out environmental impact studies in the Amazon jungle ahead of CGC oil production. They were contracted out to CGC by U.S. firm Walsh.
The tribe had demanded a ransom of $2 million to free the hostages and as compensation for what they considered to be the theft of ecological information.

Indigenous leader Miguel Vargas said on Friday his tribe would free the scientists after the oil company agreed to suspend its oil exploitation plans in the Sahime territory controlled by the Ashuar and pay them $1,300 to cover the cost of caring for the men while they were held hostage.
There was no immediate comment from CGC about the agreement.
